query: Prior calculations on concentrated alloys examined variations in atomic mass and force constants, temperature-dependent lattice heat transport, or DFT-derived elastic properties coupled to analytical conductivity estimates; some estimates require a Debye temperature. The cited simulations generally represented perfect, defect-free bulk crystals. Experiments below 200 K indicate that lattice and electronic contributions in HfNbTaTiZr can be comparable, while measurements from 300 to 1200 K on a specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen report total conductivity of 10–17 W/(K m). Available analytical approaches do not capture all relevant atomic-scale complexity in refractory high-entropy alloys, and separate transport studies do not establish a predictive solution for this alloy. Given these constraints, what testable hypothesis could an unspecified new predictive approach make for HfNbTaTiZr without conflating lattice and electronic heat transport? Explain why it should outperform earlier approaches, quantify the expected improvement, define its temperature and sample applicability limits, identify supporting observations from the cited work, and specify decisive comparisons with low- and high-temperature measurements that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: A hybrid ab-initio + machine-learning (ML) framework that (i) samples chemically-disordered HfNbTaTiZr supercells with a local‐environment ML interatomic potential and computes their Green–Kubo phonon heat flux, and (ii) adds an independently calculated KKR-CPA electronic term, will predict the lattice (κlat) and electronic (κel) thermal conductivities separately such that the total κtot = κlat + κel matches experimental values for oxygen-lean (≤0.1 wt %) polycrystalline HfNbTaTiZr within ±15 % over 300–1200 K. This accuracy will exceed that of earlier Debye, VCA or mass/force-constant–only models, which err by ≥50 % at 300–800 K.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy, single-phase bcc solid solution, grain size ≥10 µm, total interstitial content (O, N, C) ≤0.1 wt %, negligible prior deformation.
generation.intervention: Apply the proposed hybrid approach: (1) train a local-environment ML potential on DFT energies/forces of ~2000 special-quasi-random and short-range-ordered structures; (2) perform Green–Kubo molecular dynamics of 5 ps at each T for κlat; (3) compute κel(T) from KKR-CPA electronic structure and the Wiedemann–Franz relation with calculated L(T). Combine κlat and κel for κtot.
generation.conditions: Temperature 300–1200 K, vacuum or inert atmosphere to suppress oxidation, zero external pressure. Polycrystalline coupons with thickness ≥1 mm to minimise surface scattering.
generation.structural_mediator: Short-range chemical order and the associated distribution of bond stiffnesses and atomic masses that govern phonon scattering lengths; d-band electronic density of states at EF that sets the electron-phonon scattering rate.
generation.mechanism: Explicit sampling of local mass+force-constant disorder in MD captures strong phonon localization and resonant scattering absent in analytic Debye/VCA schemes, while KKR-CPA accounts for electronic disorder scattering separately; summing the two avoids double counting and prevents conflating lattice and electronic channels.
generation.predicted_outcome: For oxygen-lean samples: κlat ≈ 6 ± 1 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 300 K, falling roughly as 1/T to ≈2 ± 0.5 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 1200 K; κel ≈ 4 ± 1 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 300 K with weak T-dependence (≈3–4 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 1200 K). Thus κtot ≈10 ± 1.5 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 300 K and 5 ± 1 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 1200 K, tracking the lower envelope of reported 10–17 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ data and staying within 15 % of new measurements.
generation.baseline: Debye-based or VCA plus empirical mixing-rule models that predict κlat ≳15 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 300 K and miss the experimentally observed plateau/weak T-dependence of κtot by ≥50 %.
generation.boundary: Prediction valid only for: (a) 300 K ≤ T ≤ 1200 K; (b) impurity O, N, C ≤0.1 wt %; (c) grain size ≥10 µm (to suppress boundary scattering). Below 200 K quantum corrections and impurity-assisted phonon scattering dominate, and above 1200 K oxidation and incipient melting introduce extrinsic effects.
generation.uncertainty: Main sources: unknown degree of chemical short-range order, possible oxygen segregation at grain boundaries, and ML potential transferability above 1100 K. Combined they yield an estimated ±15 % uncertainty window on κtot.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr ingots: (i) high-purity (≤0.05 wt % O) and (ii) oxygen-contaminated (≈1 wt % O, matching prior study). HIP-forge to ≥10 µm grains. Measure κlat via laser flash analysis with in-plane thermoreflectance (for thin disks) or 3ω (for bars) while determining electrical resistivity ρ(T) for κel = L(T)T/ρ. Compare κlat, κel, and κtot to predictions at 300, 600, 900, 1200 K.
measurements: Thermal diffusivity α(T) and heat capacity C_p(T) to obtain κtot
Direct separation of κlat and κel via Wiedemann–Franz law
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if for the high-purity specimen at any temperature between 300 and 1200 K the absolute deviation |κtot_pred − κtot_exp| exceeds 15 % or if κlat_pred trends downward with 1/T while κlat_exp shows an opposite or flat dependence beyond experimental uncertainty (±10 %).
